### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**18** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c88467d4adc417e668474e1b6198a5a7c503ac3f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `376dda72d22d755f4ddbb994c643bac9f4154027` — the merge of head `0c0e86d0de94111c0c4951867e75a58ea58745fe` into base `c88467d4adc417e668474e1b6198a5a7c503ac3f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 376dda72d22d755f4ddbb994c643bac9f4154027 && git checkout 376dda72d22d755f4ddbb994c643bac9f4154027
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c88467d4adc417e668474e1b6198a5a7c503ac3f 0c0e86d0de94111c0c4951867e75a58ea58745fe && git checkout -B drift-repro c88467d4adc417e668474e1b6198a5a7c503ac3f && git merge --no-ff 0c0e86d0de94111c0c4951867e75a58ea58745fe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c88467d4adc417e668474e1b6198a5a7c503ac3f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0c0e86d0de94111c0c4951867e75a58ea58745fe`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/index.ts, packages/spec/src/data/unique-null-distinct-conformance.ts + packages/spec/src/data/unique-null-distinct-conformance.test.ts, scripts/check-driver-conformance.mjs, .changeset/29377-unique-null-distinct-conformance.md, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, packages/spec/src/data/value-roundtrip-conformance.ts, packages/spec/src/data/readable-ids-conformance.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, packages/types/src/unique-violation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-unique-constraint.ts, packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-schema.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-unique-null-distinct.test.ts, packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.ts

Inputs: card #29377 (body, triage 6580288651, claim 6580621062, dev report 6583225788, claim amendment 6583274684, Decision-needed 6583288338), PR #29509 body and files, the net diff `origin/main...0c0e86d0` (7 files, +594/−6, merge-base `6af3d295`), the head's check-runs, and the cited code on `origin/main` @ `c88467d4`. Read-only: no worktree, build, test or gate was run; the seat's conclusions were not an input to any judgment below.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff makes, each judged:

1. **Four new exports under `@objectstack/spec` (`data` entry): `UNIQUE_NULL_DISTINCT_CASES`, `UNIQUE_NULL_DISTINCT_OBJECTS`, `UniqueNullDistinctCase`, `uniqueNullDistinctDivergence` — correct.** `export *` added to `data/index.ts` between `value-roundtrip-conformance` and `date-macros.zod`, with a comment in the siblings' shape; `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` each gain exactly those four names and nothing else. No collision: `git grep` on `origin/main` for the four names and for `unique-null-distinct` finds only the driver-mongodb test file's path. `UniqueScope`/`UniqueScopeSchema` are different names. Spelling mirrors `VALUE_ROUNDTRIP_CASES` / `VALUE_ROUNDTRIP_FIELDS` / `ValueRoundTripCase` / `valueRoundTripDivergence` role for role.
2. **Every case row is a measured value or a control — holds against the drivers' code as it reads on `main`.**
   - `driver-memory`: `uniqueKeyOf` returns `null` (exempt) when any non-null-safe key part is `null` OR `undefined`; a declared index with `unique: 'global'` becomes `columns` verbatim with `nullSafeColumns: []`; a field-level `unique: 'global'` becomes `scopeField: null`, whose constant platform part folds but the field part exempts. `toStoredRecord` strips undefined own keys and fills no defaults, so an absent `code`/`tag` stays absent. All ten rows follow: `single_*` admitted/refused as tabled, `compound_one_null`, `compound_leading_null`, `compound_one_absent` admitted, `compound_equal` refused, `compound_differs_in_one_part` admitted. The refusal carries `code: 'UNIQUE_VIOLATION'`, which `isUniqueViolationError` reads on the `codes` channel.
   - `driver-sql`: `uniqueIndexesFromFields` keeps `unique: 'global'` single-column; `normalizeDeclaredIndex` keeps `unique: 'global'` listed verbatim with no `nullSafeColumns`, and `syncDeclaredIndexes` then emits `table.unique(columns)` — a plain SQL UNIQUE, NULL-distinct on SQLite, Postgres (default NULLS DISTINCT) and MySQL. An omitted column inserts NULL. `indexedKeyColumns` includes both the field-level and the declared-index columns, so the three `text` columns are sized by `keyableTextLength` (VARCHAR) and are keyable on MySQL — the fixture will not trip `explainUnkeyableTextColumn` when the suite runs the dialect matrix. Refusals: `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE` / `23505` / `ER_DUP_ENTRY` are all in the predicate.
   - `driver-mongodb`: since #29339 both `if (field.unique)` and `Boolean(idx.unique)` route through `nullDistinctUniqueOps`, a `partialFilterExpression` of `$type: NON_NULL_BSON_TYPES` on EVERY key part; `create()` strips undefined own keys, so an absent part is a missing field and an explicit `null` is BSON null — both outside the index. So `compound_one_null`, `compound_leading_null`, `compound_one_absent` are admitted by the index shape, not by luck. The E11000 refusal is recognised by `isUniqueViolationError` on the `message` channel (`duplicate key`), not by code 11000 — the docblock's "the one place that recognises all of them" holds, by that channel.
   - **"Absent behaves as null" is right on all three** (memory `undefined`, SQL NULL, Mongo missing field) and `''` is a value on all three (memory JSON-encodes `""`, SQL compares it, Mongo indexes a `string`).
   - **The compound row is true for memory, sql and mongodb as the code reads today.** Note (not a defect): #29339's real-mongod suite declared its index as bare `unique: true` and its field as `unique: true`; the case-set spells `'global'`. `mongodb-schema.ts` materialises both spellings identically, so the six cited readings transfer; the docblock could say so in one clause. Second wording nit: the docblock says the composite "`UNIQUE (region, tag)` was measured on SQLite in #13239" — the #13239 measurement quoted in `memory-unique-constraint.ts` is `UNIQUE (account_id, code)`, the same shape under other column names.
3. **The cases are expressible by a driver suite without guessing.** Object shapes are complete `syncSchema` inputs; `ObjectSchema.safeParse` accepts both (the test pins it; `label` is auto-generated by the schema). The unique declaration is stated on both surfaces, both `'global'`, so the bare-`true` inversion between field and declared index (ADR-0120 D1, `memory-unique-constraint.ts`) cannot bite, and `'global'` needs no tenant column on any driver. The refusal shape is delegated to `isUniqueViolationError` from `@objectstack/types`, the predicate every driver's refusal already satisfies; the recipe says a non-recognised error is a failure of the case, not a refusal. Every non-NULL key value is unique to one case (`und-*` prefixes; pinned by the test), so one synced pair of objects serves all ten.
4. **`uniqueNullDistinctDivergence` judges correctly, and a wrong driver cannot pass it.** It requires BOTH the second write's answer AND the stored count (2 for admitted, 1 for refused). The judge does not take the first write's outcome, but a refused first write leaves the count at 0 or 1 against the expectation in every row, so it cannot pass silently; the recipe also states step 1 must be admitted. The six wrong readings in the test each fail at least one row (sparse index → the three two-nulls rows; null/absent fold → the three absent rows; `''` as NULL → exactly `single_empty_string`; first-column compound → `compound_differs_in_one_part`; not enforced and refuse-and-keep → exactly the three refused rows). Coverage gap, not a must-fix: there is no `compound_empty_string` row, so a driver that folds `''` onto NULL only on multi-column keys is not caught; the card does not ask for it and no driver was measured to do it — a follow-up row for an adoption card.
5. **Census registration is right.** `discoverCaseSets` matches `^export const ([A-Z0-9_]*_CASES)\b` in `*-conformance.ts`: it finds `UNIQUE_NULL_DISTINCT_CASES` and only that (`_OBJECTS` does not match), and the new `CASE_SETS` row names it, so CLASSIFIED holds in both directions. `coveringFiles` scores a cell covered when a file under the driver's `src/` imports that marker from `@objectstack/spec/data` in one statement and references it outside the import (comments masked) — a suite that imports the marker will be seen. The six `LEDGER` rows carry `driver`, `marker`, `kind: 'DEBT'`, `why`, `issue`, the fields `audit()` and the summary printer read; every `driver` is a real `packages/drivers/driver-*` package (memory, mongodb, odata, sql, sqlite-wasm, turso — the whole discovered axis), so RECONCILED holds. No self-test pins `LEDGER.length`; the diff does not touch the self-test.
6. **The six DEBT rows are measured and honest.** memory and sql rows cite 10/10 in-process on `f95d0dba`; mongodb cites the six real-mongod rows of #29339 and names the server-free half its suite still owes (#5517); odata, sqlite-wasm and turso say "Not measured" and say why. Each row says the SUITE is what is missing, which is what CONSUMED measures. The ledger history note is the FILTER_TEXT shape and says so.
7. **`odata` DEBT rather than EXEMPT is right for this PR.** `ODataDriver.syncSchema` is a no-op, and the existing odata conformance suite runs the case-sets over an in-process fake service (READABLE_IDS as a loud refusal, VALUE_ROUNDTRIP via create/find). Nothing about this driver's handling of a NULL unique key has been measured, and the census header says EXEMPT is a measured claim, not a default. The card's "then the rest" puts odata adoption in the drivers' lane, where the suite or an EXEMPT row is decided on a measurement.
8. **Docblock honesty.** It states which rows were run on which driver, which four mongodb rows are derived from the index shape and not run, that the update door and the scope axis are deliberately absent, and that the drivers' suites are the measurement for the rest. It does not advertise adoption that has not happened; the test file's header says the table executes against a reference store because no driver runs it yet.
9. **Test.** Vitest-only imports, relative `./object.zod` and `./unique-null-distinct-conformance` (no cross-package reads, nothing for `check:cross-package-test-inputs`). Types: `UNIQUE_NULL_DISTINCT_OBJECTS.unique_null_compound.indexes[0].fields` is `readonly ['region','tag']` under `as const`, assignable to `readonly string[]`. Nit: `KEY_PARTS.unique_null_single` is hand-written `['code']` while the compound half is derived from the fixture.
10. **No runtime logic enters `packages/spec`.** Constants, an interface, a pure comparison of `(case, second, stored)` answering a string or `null` — the `valueRoundTripDivergence` shape.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec`: `patch`. Changeset `.changeset/29377-unique-null-distinct-conformance.md` and the PR body (round 2) both declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the two agree with the card's claim amendment 6583274684. Four new exports under a published `exports` entry widen the public surface, so `yes (widening)` is the right value (the card's original `Clause-②: no` was the seat's own claim line, corrected before review); no authorable key, value or type changes, so `none` is right; AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 grades a non-protocol widening `patch`, and `check-changeset-no-major` pins `yes (widening)` beside `none` as `patch`. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed (nothing retired, nothing narrowed). Level, declarations and body are consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open question 1 (four public names): answered — accept as spelled.** No collision on `main`; each name mirrors a sibling's role; the census only discovers `*_CASES`, so the marker name is forced.
- **Dev open question 2 / seat's "Decision needed" (six DEBT rows, options A/B/C): the maintainer's call. Landability per option, judged on the tree:**
  - **A — accept the six rows:** landable on this head as reviewed; this record is the Clause-② PASS. Each adoption PR deletes its row with its suite (RECONCILED reds a row kept beside a suite).
  - **B — enrol sql, memory and mongodb in this PR:** not landable on this head; it is a new head with driver-package files outside the claim's file surface, and this record would not cover it. Two mechanical consequences the option carries: the mongodb suite needs a server-free half (its real-mongod suites are opt-in since #5517, so an opt-in-only suite is honest about less than its green says), and the driver-sql suite must be routed through `DIALECT_CELLS` or the census reds MATRIXED on that cell.
  - **C — land the case-set without registering it:** not landable as phrased. CLASSIFIED's reverse direction reds any `*-conformance.ts` under `spec/src/data` that exports a `*_CASES` const not named in `CASE_SETS`, so deleting the `CASE_SETS` row and the six `LEDGER` rows turns `check:driver-conformance` red on this file. C requires renaming the file off the `-conformance.ts` suffix (leaving the house pattern and the card's "Done when" rows 1 and 2) or changing the census; neither is in the card.
- **Dev open question 3 (odata DEBT vs EXEMPT): answered — DEBT, see ① item 7.**
- **Dev deviation — driver-mongodb not measured live:** disclosed in the docblock, the ledger row and the PR body; four rows are derived from the pinned index shape and declared derived. Honest, not a must-fix.
- **Ledger growth is marked `⛔ MAINTAINER-ONLY` by the census itself:** this PR's rows are what the card asks for, and the Decision-needed comment puts the question to the maintainer; this record does not stand in for that agreement.
- **Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-02T17:17Z:** completed and green — Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Auto Label, Flag docs affected, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Lint · ESLint, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Type Check · source gates, Check Changeset (one attempt cancelled by a re-run, the re-run green); none red; still `in_progress` — the other Lint lanes, Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Test Core 1–8 of 8, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI. The verdict below is on the tree; landing still waits for the required ten contexts to conclude `success` (an `in_progress` is not a pass).
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]` via the relay; no off-relay login to name.

### ④ Design judgment

- `packages/spec/src/data/unique-null-distinct-conformance.ts` against the card's "Done when" and the drivers it cites: the four required rows are present (two nulls both insert; absent behaves as null; equal non-null values collide with the driver's own refusal; compound key with one NULL member does not collide), the compound row was measured on two drivers and read off the third's pinned index shape before being written, and the controls (`''`, equal compound, differs-in-one-part) are what make a non-enforcing or first-column-keyed driver fail. One axis (which NULLs a unique key admits), as every sibling table keeps one axis; the scope axis and the update door are named out with reasons. The judge is shared for the reason `valueRoundTripDivergence` is. Holds.
- `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts` against the barrel's convention: one `export *` with a provenance comment, placed with the other conformance tables. Holds.
- `scripts/check-driver-conformance.mjs` (read as the gate that enforces the rule the case-set states): the row and the six entries are the FILTER_TEXT shape, each entry measured or marked unmeasured, with the clearing rule written where the next author reads it. Holds.
- Non-blocking follow-ups for the adoption cards, not this PR: a `compound_empty_string` row once a driver is measured for it; the update door once memory and sql are measured; one clause noting that #29339's readings were taken under bare `true`, which mongodb materialises as `'global'`.
